assessments.subject: Joseph searches bags and retrieves cup from brother's bag
assessments.evidence: Genesis 44:12 explicitly searches eldest to youngest and finds goblet in Benjamin's sack. Qur'an describes search and retrieval but adds divine planning and a legal distinction absent from Genesis.

assessments.subject: Brothers allege Joseph had stolen before; Joseph keeps response inward
assessments.relationship: loose confrontation setting, no specific accusation parallel
assessments.evidence: Genesis recounts the brothers' return and Judah's confession, not an accusation that Joseph previously stole; a verse-specific primary parallel is not established.

assessments.subject: Brothers request substitute for Benjamin because of aged father
assessments.evidence: Genesis 44:33 specifically has Judah offer himself as slave instead of Benjamin, with an extended plea about their father. Qur'an's plea is briefer and asks Joseph to take one of the brothers in Benjamin's place.

assessments.subject: Joseph refuses to detain anyone other than the one possessing the cup
assessments.evidence: Genesis 44:17 refuses to enslave the others and retains only the possessor of the goblet. Qur'an frames the refusal as avoiding injustice; legal wording and motivations differ.

assessments.subject: Eldest brother remains behind and invokes pledge to father
assessments.evidence: Genesis 44:32 records Judah's pledge and 44:33-34 his offer to remain in Benjamin's place; it does not recount the Qur'anic consultation and eldest brother staying in Egypt.

dossier.title: Joseph's cup, Benjamin's detention and the brothers' plea
dossier.comparative_summary: Genesis 44:11–34 and Qur'an 12:76–80 share the discovery of the cup, a plea motivated by their father's distress and refusal to detain another brother. Genesis develops Judah's long plea and voluntary substitution; the Qur'an includes Joseph's private response to an accusation of prior theft, divine planning and the eldest brother's decision to remain. Distinct narrative details cannot be treated as proof of textual dependence.
